terms.definition: The control center of the cell — a membrane-bound organelle that stores the DNA and directs cell activity.
terms.function: Protects the DNA and decides which instructions are used to keep the cell running.
terms.whereItIs: Usually near the center of eukaryotic cells.
terms.whyItMatters: Without it, the cell would have no organized plan for dividing, growing, or making proteins.

terms.definition: A double membrane that wraps the nucleus and separates it from the cytoplasm.
terms.function: Controls what enters and leaves through its pores.
terms.whereItIs: Around the entire nucleus as its outer boundary.
terms.whyItMatters: It keeps the genetic material protected and organized.

terms.definition: An opening in the nuclear envelope that lets molecules move between nucleus and cytoplasm.
terms.function: Selective passage of RNA and proteins.
terms.whereItIs: Scattered across the nuclear envelope surface.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the nucleus send instructions out while keeping the DNA safe.

terms.definition: A dense region inside the nucleus that assembles the parts used to make ribosomes.
terms.function: Produces the RNA components of ribosomes.
terms.whereItIs: Floating within the nucleus, usually one or a few dark spots.
terms.whyItMatters: It links the nucleus to protein production in the cell.

terms.definition: A cell without a membrane-bound nucleus, like a bacterium; its DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm.
terms.function: Serves as the simplest organisms that read DNA directly in the cytoplasm.
terms.whyItMatters: It distinguishes bacteria from all eukaryotic cells.
